headline: A German study finds AI has not yet cost the country many jobs, but full-time employment among workers under 30 is falling behind in the most AI-affected occupations.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a research institute's data on jobs and AI, relevant and balanced, but read only through a short wire report and showing a relative gap, not a cause.
importance_line: Workers under 30 in the most AI-affected jobs are the group showing early weakness, while mid-career workers have fared better, but the short report gives no job totals and compares groups of occupations, so it does not show that AI caused the gap.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports, in a wire story citing the study, that the Institute for Employment Research (IAB) in Nuremberg, the research arm of Germany's Federal Employment Agency, found AI has yet to cost Germany a significant number of jobs: since 2022, employment in heavily AI-affected occupations grew almost six percentage points more among 30- to 39-year-olds, and around five points more among 40- to 64-year-olds, than in less affected occupations. For workers under 30, however, full-time employment in heavily AI-affected occupations fell 1.2 percentage points more than in less affected jobs, and the researchers see fundamental risks from AI in industry, particularly in non-academic occupations.
notes: Read on Yahoo Finance, a copy site; the text has no byline and only the photo is credited to dpa, so the wire agency is probably dpa but this is not stated for the text, hence the credit 'Yahoo Finance, citing the IAB'. A search for another outlet carrying the story found none. The IAB report itself was not opened.
